tests.environment: macOS isolated synthetic PostgreSQL 17 on 127.0.0.1:55492 (flowboard_access_test); API 383 pass, contracts 41 pass, 0 skipped

security.reason: Authority matrix, origin/CSRF (origin.ts, app.ts:97), Google callback (google-auth.ts:165-167, state check before session), admin secret (admin-secret.ts, system.ts), dev-login closure (session.ts:103) and cookie policy hold on the probes run. Replay, revoked, cross-site and never-granted probes gave 404/403 with no leak. Deductions: anonymous board existence oracle (R3-08), committed local harness credential string (R3-13), raw session IDs (R3-10). None is a confirmed exploitable defect.

correctness.reason: Happy paths and role limits pass in 383 API and 41 contract tests. Under concurrency, comment PATCH and DELETE (R3-01) and import commit against the same import (R3-02) return 503 in 10/10 forced rounds, so those claimed writes do not complete under parallel use. Stale 404 message split and anonymous 401/404 split (R3-08, R3-15) are minor.

integrity.reason: No lost or duplicate write observed: the deadlocked transaction rolls back (only the 200 side commits) and replays after revocation return 404 with no saved body (replay probe). Lock-order inversions remain in comment PATCH/DELETE and import commit (R3-01, R3-02), against the criterion that no deadlock occurs and no inversion is introduced. Cards and comments POST and card create/move are board-first and clean (P3, P5, P6).

tests.reason: Suite is complete and real: 383/41 pass, 0 skipped, isolated PostgreSQL. Forced probes and replay probe were run by the reviewer. Gaps: the only mounted interleaving test is a random 8-round loop and covers comment POST only (its pre-fix failure is 3/3, so it detects the regression, R3-04); replay-after-revocation is tested for one route in the suite (R3-03); no forced test exists for PATCH/DELETE or import commit races.

maintainability.reason: Lock-order protocol is written down in rbac.ts and board-grants-foundation.ts, and most routes follow it. Misleading comments (R3-05, R3-06): unmounted/do-not-deploy notes contradict mounted code, FOR SHARE comments with no lock, and "draft" modules that are mounted (board-access-cursor-draft.ts via routes/board-grants.ts:8-12). Minimum reached, not exceeded.

operations.reason: Retryable 503 with Retry-After for 40P01/40001 (error-handler.ts:145-152) with no internal text leak; body limit, deadline, no-store headers, per-request single-connection pool in worker.ts. Gaps: no measured performance; deployed CURSOR_SECRET absent so the access list fails closed with 503 (R3-07); dependency advisory status unverified (no network).

findings.description: Comment PATCH and DELETE lock the card row before the board row. routes/comments.ts:199 (PATCH) and :310 (DELETE) run SELECT ... FOR SHARE OF cd before checkOrReplayProjectWriteReceipt, which takes the board row FOR UPDATE (rbac.ts:397-398). Card update and move take the board first, then the card FOR UPDATE (adapters/cards.ts:497-508 and :704-714). Forced repro: reviewer-r3-forced-probes.ts P1 (move first, PATCH second) and P2 (move first, DELETE second): 10/10 rounds each return 200 for the move and 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE for the comment request. pg_stat_database deadlocks delta is 30 over the run (P1+P2+P4).
findings.rationale: Criterion 10 requires that parallel writes on one board never deadlock and that no lock-order inversion is introduced. The 503 is a retryable error, not a 500, and the aborted transaction rolls back. The POST route was fixed (P6 201/200 10/10, no deadlock), but PATCH and DELETE still use the card-first order. Blocking because it contradicts a mandatory criterion.
findings.impact: A comment edit or delete that overlaps a card move or update on the same card fails with a retryable 503 instead of completing. No data is lost or duplicated.
findings.counterevidence: Retry-After 503 (error-handler.ts:145-152), no 500; comment POST is fixed (P6); reviewer found no failure on the revocation path.
findings.recommendedFix: Take acquireWriteGrantLock and acquireWritableProjectContextLock (board FOR UPDATE) before the card-row lock in PATCH and DELETE, as routes/comments.ts:107-110 does for POST; add forced PATCH and DELETE regression tests modelled on P1 and P2.

findings.description: Import commit against the same import, twice in parallel, deadlocks. routes/imports.ts:222 takes card_imports FOR SHARE before the board lock; checkOrReplayProjectWriteReceipt (imports.ts:234) then takes the board FOR UPDATE; commitCardImport upgrades the same import row FOR UPDATE (adapters/imports.ts:808), which waits on the other commit share lock while that commit waits on the board. Forced repro: P4 in reviewer-r3-forced-probes.ts, 10/10 rounds (200, 503). Import commit against card create (P5) and card move on the same board show no deadlock (200/409 10/10).
findings.rationale: Same class as R3-01 (card or import row locked before the board), so it contradicts criterion 10. Not a duplicate effect: the import had no rows in the probe, so card duplication under a real commit is unproved (coverage gap).
findings.impact: A double-submitted commit gets a retryable 503 rather than the adapter's intended COMMIT_IN_PROGRESS conflict. One commit still succeeds.
findings.counterevidence: 503 is retryable; the aborted transaction rolls back; commit vs create/move is clean (P5).
findings.recommendedFix: Lock the import row only after the board lock (drop the pre-check FOR SHARE, or read the scope without a lock), or lock the import row FOR UPDATE before the board in every commit path. Add a forced commit-vs-commit test with imported rows and assert exactly one set of cards.

findings.description: Replay-after-revocation is covered by one mounted test only (comment-move-replay.test.ts:69, comment POST). The reviewer probe (reviewer-r3-replay-probe.ts) shows that card create, card move, card PATCH and comment POST replays after revocation return 404 with no saved body (log). Trash delete/restore, comment PATCH/DELETE, image and import replays have no mounted test.
findings.rationale: Criterion 5 lists replay among the mounted-handler cases. Missing coverage is unproved, not a pass (the R2 rule). The four probed routes behave correctly; the other routes use the same helper, which checks the grant before replay (idempotency.ts:53-64), but that is source evidence only.
findings.impact: Regression risk only; the current code path returns 404 with no body for the probed routes.
findings.counterevidence: Probe: 4/4 routes return 404 after revocation, no leak; idempotency.ts:53-64 checks the grant before the receipt.
findings.recommendedFix: Add mounted replay-after-revocation tests for trash, comment PATCH/DELETE, image attach and import commit, using the same harness as reviewer-r3-replay-probe.ts.

findings.description: The mounted interleaving test (comment-move-replay.test.ts:40-67) is a random 8-round Promise.all loop, not a forced ordering. It asserts a database-wide pg_stat_database deadlock delta. It fails on the pre-fix code in 3/3 runs (reviewer-r3-old-code-comment-move-test.log), so it detects the R2-01 class, but it covers only comment POST and cannot prove absence.
findings.rationale: Test quality, not an acceptance failure. Counterevidence: the test does catch the pre-fix 503 reliably in this environment.
findings.reproduction: pre-fix copy of e32f837 with this test: 3/3 runs fail with unexpected status 503 (reviewer-r3-old-code-comment-move-test.log)
findings.impact: Regressions in PATCH/DELETE ordering would not be caught by this test.
findings.counterevidence: On current HEAD the test passes (complete-suite log).
findings.recommendedFix: Add forced-ordering tests (helper holding the board row, as in reviewer-r3-forced-probes.ts) for PATCH, DELETE and import commit once R3-01 and R3-02 are fixed.

findings.description: routes/cards.ts:152 and :227 say "Lock card row FOR SHARE to serialize against concurrent trash/delete (F-05)", but the statement is a plain SELECT with no lock. The real serialization is the FOR UPDATE in adapters/cards.ts:508 and :714, with a state re-check at :517 and :723.
findings.rationale: Misleading comment. Counterevidence: no integrity defect found; the adapter re-checks state after taking the lock.
findings.impact: Future maintainers may remove the adapter re-check believing the route lock exists.
findings.counterevidence: adapters/cards.ts:517 and :723 re-check card state after FOR UPDATE.
findings.recommendedFix: Correct the comments or add the lock.

findings.description: Stale documentation contradicts mounted code. board-grants-foundation.ts:1-14 says the module is unmounted and existing routes do not use it, but boards.ts, comments.ts, trash.ts and board-grants.ts call it. services/board-access-cursor-draft.ts:2-6 says "Unmounted cursor experiment", yet routes/board-grants.ts:8-12 mounts GET /boards/:boardId/access. database/migrations/0007_board_grants.sql:1-9 (and the embedded copy at embedded-migrations.ts:42) says "Do not deploy until every board-derived route is converted" and "Existing routes do not" follow the lock order.
findings.rationale: Maintainability and review risk (carried R2-05). A future reader may treat mounted authorization as unfinished or skip a lock review.
findings.counterevidence: Mounted usage verified in app.ts and routes files.
findings.recommendedFix: Update the header comments and the 0007 header to describe the mounted state, and rename the "draft" modules that serve mounted routes.

findings.description: GET /api/v1/boards/:boardId/access returns 503 CONFIG_ERROR for every caller when CURSOR_SECRET is unset, because apps/api/wrangler.jsonc sets no CURSOR_SECRET (top level, dev or uat). The configuration check runs before the Owner check (getCursorSecret at routes/board-grants.ts:28-35 is called at :52, and the Owner check is inside lockOwnedBoard afterwards). Probe: owner 503, member 503 (reviewer-r3-small-probes.log).
findings.rationale: Fails closed and discloses no board data, but the Owner cannot read the access list in a deployed runtime. Not one of the frozen criteria, so non-blocking; it is an Owner-administration functional gap.
findings.impact: Access list endpoint unusable in deployed runtimes; a non-Owner gets 503 rather than a private 404.
findings.counterevidence: No board data is returned; source confirms the secret is required (>= 32 bytes).
findings.recommendedFix: Provision CURSOR_SECRET per environment as a secret, and check Owner status before reading configuration.

findings.description: Anonymous GET /api/v1/boards/:boardId returns 401 for an existing board and 404 for a missing one (routes/boards.ts:145-151: existence check at :145 before getActorOrThrow). Probe: 401 vs 404 (reviewer-r3-small-probes.log P1).
findings.rationale: Carried R2-02. Anonymous callers can tell existing board IDs apart. IDs are random (brd_ + UUID), so the practical risk is low. Criterion 3 names revoked and never-granted actors, not anonymous callers.
findings.impact: Existence oracle for anonymous callers who already hold a board ID.
findings.counterevidence: Authenticated outsiders get 404 for both cases.
findings.recommendedFix: Authenticate first, or return the same 401 for anonymous callers regardless of board existence.

findings.description: Card GET and image reads check the board grant in autocommit statements and deliver afterwards (adapters/cards.ts:459 and :476 via requireCardBoardAccess on the bare pool; adapters/images.ts requireImageBoardAccess on the pool). A revocation committed after the check and before delivery is not blocked for that response (carried R2-03).
findings.rationale: Single in-flight response window; other board reads hold the grant through delivery (suite tests named "holds its grant until delivery"). Not a frozen-criteria failure, because the check precedes delivery.
findings.reproduction: source read; not probed in R3
findings.impact: One response can complete after a revocation committed during it.
findings.counterevidence: Check happens before any private field is returned.
findings.recommendedFix: Use lockBoardAccess (grant FOR SHARE) inside a transaction for these reads, as the list reads do.

findings.description: Session IDs are stored and looked up as raw bearer tokens (adapters/session.ts:127 INSERT id; lookup by id). Carried DR1-05 and R2-07.
findings.rationale: Hardening item, not exploitable without database read access. Outside the frozen criteria.
findings.impact: A database read exposes live session tokens.
findings.counterevidence: Cookies are HttpOnly and Secure off localhost.
findings.recommendedFix: Store SHA-256 of the token and compare on lookup.

findings.description: Google sign-in overwrites display_name on every login (routes/google-auth.ts:188-195) and creates a personal workspace for every first login, including invitees (google-auth.ts:207-215). Carried DR1-04 and R2-06.
findings.rationale: Product decision outside board access. Recorded for Architect.
findings.impact: Profile names change on each sign-in; invitees get an unused workspace.
findings.counterevidence: None needed.
findings.recommendedFix: Architect decision: preserve user-edited name; create the default workspace only when no invitation applies.

findings.description: Origin check and credentialed CORS trust any http://localhost:* or 127.0.0.1 origin in every runtime, including the deployed Worker (origin.ts:7-11, 20-22; app.ts:53). Carried R2-08.
findings.rationale: Allowed by criterion 8 (localhost is an explicit trusted origin). Lax cookies are not sent on cross-site POST, so a page on another site cannot use the session through localhost.
findings.impact: None beyond the allowed localhost trust.
findings.counterevidence: Cross-site POST from a foreign origin returns 403 (small probe P3).
findings.recommendedFix: Optional: trust localhost only outside the Worker runtime.

findings.description: apps/api/wrangler.jsonc:12 includes a localConnectionString with a password for the 127.0.0.1 harness database (flowboard_local_only). It is used by wrangler dev --local only and is not a deployed variable.
findings.rationale: Local harness credential, not a real secret. Recorded so it is not reused elsewhere.
findings.counterevidence: Bound to 127.0.0.1; not in vars.
findings.recommendedFix: Move local connection strings to a gitignored .dev.vars file.

findings.description: Anonymous and never-granted callers get distinct 404 messages for a missing card or import versus an existing one without a grant ("Card not found." from routes/comments.ts:99-101 vs "Board not found." from rbac.ts:357 via acquireWriteGrantLock). Card and import IDs are random UUIDs.
findings.rationale: Existence signal for callers who already hold a card ID. Criterion 3 requires non-enumerating responses; IDs make practical enumeration unlikely, so non-blocking.
findings.counterevidence: Both responses are 404 with no board or card content.
findings.recommendedFix: Return one message for both cases.

findings.description: Carried from round 2: comment POST versus move deadlock. Status: POST part resolved (routes/comments.ts:91-110 board-first; P6 and the complete-suite test pass); PATCH and DELETE part still open as R3-01.
findings.rationale: Verified by forced probe P6 (201/200, 10/10) and the suite test at comment-move-replay.test.ts:40.
findings.counterevidence: Pre-fix copy fails 3/3 (reviewer-r3-old-code-comment-move-test.log).
findings.recommendedFix: None for POST.

findings.description: Carried from round 2: replay after revocation. Behaviour is correct for four mounted routes (replay probe); mounted test coverage is incomplete, carried as R3-03.
findings.rationale: Partially closed. Coverage gap stays open.
findings.counterevidence: See probe log.
findings.recommendedFix: See R3-03.

findings.description: Round-1 same-board create versus move deadlock. Resolved for create and move: board-first lock (rbac.ts:397-398), 15 rounds of 6 parallel creates and 6 parallel moves with no 500 (round-2 probe P1; R3 control P3 200/409 10/10).
findings.rationale: Verified by suite test "parallel writes on one board never deadlock into 500" and forced control P3.
findings.counterevidence: P3 and P5 show no deadlock.
findings.recommendedFix: None.

findings.description: Round-1 test-only admin secret reachable from a Worker bundled with NODE_ENV=test. Resolved: deployed is derived from bindings (system.ts:10,22; admin-secret.ts:12) and the Worker always binds HYPERDRIVE or DATABASE_URL (runtime/worker.ts:16). Probe: /system/status with a wrong or absent secret returns 403 in NODE_ENV=test (small probe P4).
findings.rationale: Verified by source and probe; unit test at board-concurrency.test.ts:78-82.
findings.counterevidence: Deployed path never accepts the test secret.
findings.recommendedFix: None.

findings.description: Round-1 missing Origin/CSRF check. Resolved: origin.ts wired at app.ts:97; cross-site POST returns 403 (small probe P3); null origin, Referer-only and lookalike origins rejected in R2 probe P5.
findings.rationale: Verified by source, suite (origin-check.test.ts) and probes.
findings.counterevidence: 403 on cross-site POST.
findings.recommendedFix: None.

findings.description: Round-1 embedded-migrations drift with no check. Resolved: board-concurrency.test.ts:84-91 asserts byte equality with database/migrations/*.sql and passes in the complete-suite log.
findings.rationale: Verified by test run.
findings.counterevidence: Test passes.
findings.recommendedFix: None.

findings.description: Round-1 target changed during review. Resolved for this round: start and end HEAD are 3e11ab8 and the worktree had no tracked changes at start; the only changes are untracked files under docs/reviews/BOARD-ACCESS-DELTA-20261028-R3/.
findings.rationale: Process item. Checked at start and end of the review.
findings.counterevidence: See final report.
findings.recommendedFix: None.

findings.description: Rejected candidate: Origin/CSRF bypass with null Origin, Referer-only, lookalike localhost origin, legacy cookie name, or cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site.
findings.rationale: All session-carrying variants return 403 (origin.ts:31-53; small probe P3; R2 probe P5). Requests with no Origin or Referer are accepted only when Sec-Fetch-Site is absent or same-origin (no cross-site browser request reaches the handler).
findings.counterevidence: Probe and code path.
findings.recommendedFix: None.

findings.description: Rejected candidate: trash versus move card/board deadlock (trash locks card and board in an order that can invert).
findings.rationale: routes/trash.ts takes the board through checkOrReplayProjectWriteReceipt (:61 and :193) before the adapter locks the card (adapters/trash.ts:220 and :536 after board lock at :239). Round-2 forced probe (reviewer-r2-lock-order-forced-probe.log) showed no 40P01 in 10 rounds. Not re-probed in R3.
findings.reproduction: R2 forced probe; source read in R3
findings.counterevidence: Board is taken before the card in both paths.
findings.recommendedFix: None.

findings.description: Rejected candidate: column writes (addColumn, updateColumn, reorderColumns, deleteColumn) versus Owner grant revocation deadlock.
findings.rationale: boards.ts addColumn (:366-400) and siblings take lockBoardAccess (grant FOR SHARE) before the board row FOR UPDATE, so a revocation that holds the grant row FOR UPDATE cannot hold the board row first. Source only; not probed in R3.
findings.counterevidence: Grant share is held before the board lock.
findings.recommendedFix: None.

findings.description: Rejected candidate: trash-purge worker versus card moves deadlock.
findings.rationale: services/trash-purge.ts claims card rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and never takes a board row lock, so it cannot wait on a board held by a move. Source only.
findings.counterevidence: No board lock in purge.
findings.recommendedFix: None.

findings.description: Rejected candidate: email-only dev-login reachable on the deployed Worker.
findings.rationale: routes/session.ts:103 returns 404 whenever HYPERDRIVE or DATABASE_URL is bound, and runtime/worker.ts:16 always binds one. wrangler.jsonc binds HYPERDRIVE at top level, dev and uat.
findings.counterevidence: Binding check.
findings.recommendedFix: None.
